solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Procreating? X is a sign of this

definitions.meaning: breeding, the way living things increase their numbers; the question mark flags the loose noun-for-verb fit

definitions.text: X is a sign of this
definitions.meaning: the cross symbol x is the arithmetic sign for times-ing two numbers

explanation.surface: A puzzled aside on breeding, as if an X marked the spot of reproduction.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is biological increase by breeding; the second is the arithmetic operation whose symbol is a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Biologists speak of cells and creatures increasing by breeding as this; in sums the cross symbol means times.

clue.text: Complete obsessive, scrubbing floor of kitchen?

indicators.note: scrubbing out means removing, so a letter is wiped from the word for obsessive

parts.note: a nutter is slang for a fanatic or obsessive person

indicators.note: in a down clue the floor of a word is its bottom, that is last, letter

explanation.surface: A fanatical cleaner gets so absorbed in scrubbing the kitchen floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrubbing' looks like cleaning but deletes; 'floor of kitchen' is its last letter N, taken from NUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives for total or absolute, as in an utter disaster or a complete disaster.

clue.text: Some from committee therefore develop 28 in East London

indicators.note: Some from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A committee's conclusion about developing Hampstead Heath, an open space in north London.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 is HAMPSTEAD HEATH, which in East London (Cockney) rhyming slang means teeth; so the definition is 'develop teeth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses Hampstead Heath for teeth, and a baby cutting its first teeth is said to do this.

clue.text: Landlord's supporting institute, shown in report for renovation

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: renovation means rebuilding, so the letters are taken apart and remade

explanation.surface: A landlord backing an institute is named in a report about refurbishing a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landlord' here is a proprietor in general, an owner, not only someone who lets property; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord, especially of a pub, is its owner, and owner is the plain meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Scrap minor team with regular absentees

indicators.note: regular absentees means every other letter is missing, so only alternate letters survive

explanation.surface: A lowly side fighting it out despite players who keep missing games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with regular absentees' keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of MINOR TEAM. 'Scrap' looks like a fight; it is a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny bit or jot, named after the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet, means the same as a scrap.

clue.text: Usual passion, following onset of 'Aussies against English'

indicators.note: following says the word for passion comes after the earlier pieces
the onset of a word is its start, its opening letter

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against, as in sports fixtures
rage can mean a passion or craze as well as fury

explanation.surface: The customary fervour at the start of an Ashes series, Australia versus England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onset of' gives A from 'Aussies'; 'following' puts RAGE after A V E.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical or ordinary, so the usual case is the standard, middling one.

clue.text: Reckless devil beginning to upset Elvis mimic

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
a mimic produces a distorted copy, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild impersonator of Elvis upsets people with his reckless act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to upset' is U; 'mimic' rearranges ELVIS as LSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on impulse without thought is the same as being rash or reckless.

clue.text: After new configuring, you only let Ron on your bike?

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters come after the abbreviation for new
configuring means arranging in a new layout, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A possessive cyclist who lets only Ron ride the new bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'configuring' rearranges YOU ONLY LET RON into OTONYOURNELLY after N. 'On your bike' is British slang for go away, a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang retorts meaning no way, a dismissive refusal of a request.

clue.text: Welshman turned telly on — for example, relaxing harp and organ

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name

indicators.note: turned means twisted round, so the letters of telly are rearranged
relaxing loosens the letters, so harp is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Welshman switches on the TV to unwind with harp and organ music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives LYTEL from TELLY and 'relaxing' gives RAPH from HARP. 'organ' looks musical but means a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is often called an organ, a medium of communication; this is a British national daily title.

clue.text: Max rejected army flask (not maintaining right temperature)

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: not maintaining means not keeping, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Thermos is a brand of vacuum flask

explanation.surface: Max turned down an army vacuum flask that failed to keep the drink hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Max' looks like a man's name but is short for maximum. The TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Max, short for maximum, means the highest amount, and the phrase means no more than that limit.

clue.text: Windows system in decay — someone not living at home?

indicators.note: in says the Windows version sits inside the word for decay

parts.note: to eat away is to corrode or decay
XP is a version of Microsoft's Windows operating system

explanation.surface: An old computer system rotting away, owned by someone living abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' suggests glass but is the Microsoft software; the question mark admits the definition is a loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate lives outside their native country, so not at home in a national sense.

clue.text: Hound and endlessly entice songstress

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to lure is to entice
Cher is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: Someone hounds and tempts a female singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LURE to LUR. 'Hound' looks like a verb but is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog, typically part greyhound, so a kind of hound.

clue.text: Swimmer keeping both hands in the sea

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the word for the sea holds the two letters

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
R and L are the abbreviations for right and left, the two hands

explanation.surface: A swimmer in the sea keeps both hands in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: A large game fish with a spear-like snout, so a swimmer in the cryptic-crossword sense of a fish.

clue.text: Four US leaders look so drunk, hiding nothing in Yankee college

indicators.note: hiding means concealing, so the word for drunk holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: stoned is slang for very drunk or high

indicators.note: in says the slang for nothing goes between the two letters

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: Four American presidents look drunk while hiding nothing at a US college.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all. The four leaders are the presidents carved in granite on Mount Rushmore.
explanation.definitionFit: Four presidents carved into granite on Mount Rushmore literally wear rock faces, expressionless and impassive.

clue.text: Animal's egg placed in shade

indicators.note: placed in says the egg-shaped letter goes inside the word for shade

parts.note: a shade means a tiny amount, a tad
O, shaped like an egg, stands for one

explanation.surface: An animal's egg laid in a shady spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed in' puts O inside TAD. 'shade' looks like shadow but means a touch or little bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A warty amphibian related to the frog is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Richard 'ammond starts to drive Aston Martin here in Europe

parts.note: the Top Gear presenter Richard Hammond is nicknamed the Hamster; the apostrophe drops his H, so the H goes from the nickname too

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A TV motoring presenter begins to drive an Aston Martin somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Hammond of the BBC car show Top Gear is called the Hamster; written 'ammond, his H is dropped, Cockney style.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital is a city on the European continent, the place where this drive happens.

clue.text: Old golfer to be seen with wine (French) amongst group of stars

indicators.note: amongst says the French words go inside the name of the constellation

parts.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars
être is French for to be, with (French) applying to both words
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A retired golfer spotted drinking wine among a group of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(French)' covers both 'to be' and 'wine'. 'stars' looks like celebrities but is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Trevino is a Mexican-American golfer who won six majors in the 1960s to 1980s, now long retired.

clue.text: Cryptically, lots slipped behind

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says take LOST and grind it up (ground), which rearranges it into the clue word lots

explanation.surface: Plenty of things slipped behind, a terse report of decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptically' warns this works backwards: ground (milled) is an anagram signal, so LOST ground makes LOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose ground is to fall back relative to rivals, which is falling behind.

clue.text: Windy Asian city mostly in depression moving northwards

indicators.note: in says the shortened city goes inside the reversed depression
in a down clue moving northwards means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sag is a dip or depression

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Seoul is the capital of South Korea

explanation.surface: A blustery Asian city lies in a hollow shifting north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving northwards' reverses because this is a down light, read upwards; the city is South Korea's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Windy can mean full of gas, flatulent, so vaporous or full of wind.

clue.text: Expensive letter-opener?

definitions.meaning: the word that opens a letter, as in the salutation before the name; the question mark flags it is not a paper knife

explanation.walkthrough: 'letter-opener' suggests a knife for slitting envelopes; it is the first word of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Costly goods are this in British usage, and correspondence traditionally begins with this salutation.

clue.text: Tennis professionals serve fast

parts.note: the ATP is the Association of Tennis Professionals
an ace is a serve the receiver cannot touch

explanation.surface: Tennis pros serve quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like a description of the serve but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at speed, quickly, means the same as fast.

clue.text: Don't use much sage, preparing sandwiches round yard

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the rearranged letters hold the round letter
preparing herbs means working them, so the letters of sage are rearranged

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Cooking advice: go light on the sage when making sandwiches, all round the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparing' rearranges SAGE as GEAS; 'sandwiches' puts O inside after G; Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To use sparingly, not overdo it, is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Skimmed article in newspaper, Friday Echo, repeatedly

indicators.note: in says the article goes inside the newspaper's initials

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: repeatedly says the letter is given twice

parts.note: E is Echo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A skimmed piece in Friday's Echo newspaper, read over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skimmed' looks like reading quickly but describes milk; 'repeatedly' doubles E.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimmed milk has had its cream removed, so it is free of fat.

clue.text: Proper sinister? On the contrary

definitions.meaning: sinister means left in heraldry, so its contrary is the opposite side

explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' looks like evil, but in heraldry it is the left-hand side; 'On the contrary' asks for the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct or fitting is one sense; and the opposite of sinister, left in heraldry, is the other hand side.

clue.text: Crown restored part of the taproom

indicators.note: restored is read as re-stored, put back, so the letters go backwards
part of says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A crown restored in part of the bar room of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' finds ETAP across 'the taproom'; 'restored' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of the head is its top, and this old word means the head or scalp.

clue.text: Increase insecticide within banks of Arno

indicators.note: within says the insecticide sits between the outer letters
the banks of a river are its two edges, so the outer letters

parts.note: DDT is a well-known insecticide

explanation.surface: Pesticide levels increase along the banks of the Italian river Arno.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks of' gives A and O, the outer letters of ARNO; 'within' puts DDT between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplement something is to make it bigger, the same as to increase it.

clue.text: Spiritual power martial artist Jackie displays in large building

indicators.note: in says the surname goes inside the rearranged letters
building means constructing, so the letters of large are put together anew

parts.note: Jackie Chan is the martial-arts film star

explanation.surface: Jackie Chan shows his spiritual power in a big building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun for a structure but is the anagram signal; 'displays' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief angel is a heavenly being, one of the ranks of spiritual powers in Christian tradition.

clue.text: London area is half of what politicians and former PM discussed

indicators.note: half of here takes the central two of the four letters

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Ted Heath was British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A London place name is half of what MPs said about a former Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives HA, the middle of WHAT; 'discussed' gives TEAD HEATH by sound from Ted Heath.
explanation.definitionFit: This large open heath in north London is a well-known area of the city.
